scenarios.description: The processor gains a unilateral right to process for its own purposes, defeating Art. 28(3)(a) GDPR.

clauses.text: Processing only on documented instructions from the controller, including transfers.
Authorised persons are committed to confidentiality.
Appropriate technical and organisational measures, summary available on request.
Processor may engage sub-processors at its own discretion.
Assistance with Chapter III data subject requests.
Breach notification within fourteen days; DPIA assistance where commercially agreed.
Processor may retain personal data after termination.
Annual third-party audit certificate provided to the controller.
Transfers to affiliates in third countries as necessary.
Governed by the laws of Germany.
Personal data is stored within the European Economic Area.

risk_flags.rationale: Sub-processors appointed at the processor's discretion and the controller waives its right to object, which does not meet Art. 28(3)(d) GDPR.
Indefinite retention for the processor's own purposes after termination conflicts with Art. 28(3)(g) GDPR, which requires deletion or return at the controller's choice.
A fourteen day breach notification period is long relative to the controller's own 72 hour obligation.
An annual third-party certificate is a common market position.
Transfers are limited to affiliates for service provision.

committed themselves to confidentiality
appropriate technical and organisational measures
may engage sub-processors at its own discretion
the data subject's rights laid down in Chapter III

within
fourteen (14) days of becoming aware of it
for its own legitimate business purposes
all personal data shall be stored exclusively within the European Economic Area
